title: The Fast Fashion Problem
content: Fast fashion refers to the rapid production of cheap clothing that follows the latest trends. Brands release new collections every few weeks, encouraging consumers to constantly buy new clothes and throw away older ones. While this allows people to look fashionable on a budget, it has devastating consequences. The fashion industry is one of the largest polluters in the world. Enormous amounts of water are required to grow cotton, and toxic chemicals are used to dye fabrics, often polluting rivers in developing countries. Moreover, fast fashion frequently relies on cheap labor, with garment workers enduring poor conditions and low wages. As a reaction, a "slow fashion" movement is growing, which promotes buying second-hand clothes, choosing sustainable materials, and buying fewer items of higher quality.
